shadow.note: none named on this tape; placed at the object for the graphmap

operative.label: JBHT Q3: top line +20% incl. fuel surcharges; intermodal loads +8.5% (reported 10-15)
PPI at its fastest pace in 4+ years; retail sales ex autos & gas flat (week of 10-15)
intermodal ≈65% more fuel-efficient than truck; shippers substitute and the price follows

Hormuz not flowing freely "for quite some time" (Walsh, by statement)

positions.note: declared empty, by-record: one source, one corner

positions.fluid: posts the record in order — the print, the strait, the surcharge, the loads — and never assembles it
fluidKeywords: a lot of this is oil
positions.note: aligned: zero vehicle words in seventeen lines

lines.quote: the PPI rose at its fastest pace in more than four years; retail sales ex motor vehicles and gas barely budged
lines.note: dates the week's record: price into the index, activity flat. 'Jarring' is the one adjective
lines.zWhy: price into the index, activity flat: passes

lines.quote: oil is not flowing freely in the Strait of Hormuz, and hasn't for quite some time; we're starting to see that show up in pressures — in inflation, in interest rates
lines.note: →PG01: the supply constraint named, and where it lands — the price level and the rate, not the shelf
lines.zWhy: 'shows up in inflation and interest rates' is the price channel, not the shelf

lines.quote: the US economy has been incredibly resilient until this point; I expected the signals to show up earlier than they have
lines.note: activity undented, by his own surprise. Sees the gap between the constraint and the economy; does not ask what is absorbing it

lines.quote: with diesel prices rising, you've got the inflation pressure
lines.note: the crunch named as diesel, landing as a price. Seven words
lines.zWhy: diesel named as a price pressure, nothing else

lines.quote: the concentration in the AI trade has given the market its resilience — it has survived higher rates, $100 oil
lines.note: the crunch as weather already survived: priced and passed. Oil is a clause in a sentence about something else

lines.quote: the AI trade has looked through all the geopolitical conflict; the Fed is facing weakness in employment and at the same time inflation is a problem — CPI and PPI not where we want them
lines.note: dates the Fed's bind: price up, labor soft. The crunch is one input, unnamed here
lines.zWhy: the crunch as one input to a price problem; labor soft for other reasons

lines.quote: inflation reports — a lot of this is oil; it is reverberating through, and he's going to have to be responsive to that
lines.note: THE ATTRIBUTION: the print read back to oil. The crunch reaches the Fed as a price, not a shortage — 'reverberating' is the pass-through, heard
lines.zWhy: 'reverberating through' is pass-through heard at the Fed

lines.quote: the movement of goods is being affected by the pressure consumers face and companies paying higher prices — and fuel costs, how much more companies are paying to move those goods
lines.note: fuel as a cost line on freight: the pass-through named before the earnings call
lines.zWhy: fuel as a cost line companies pay: passes

lines.quote: trucking is very much an indicator of consumer demand; pressure coming for consumers as we saw in the CPI and PPI data this week
lines.note: sets up the test without running it: if the crunch bites, trucking shows it. The nearest the tape comes to a falsifier — and it is left as a remark
lines.zWhy: a test set up, not run; leans pass because the week's data is price data

lines.quote: J.B. Hunt under pressure; earnings largely in line, $1.82; revenue about $3.69 billion
lines.zWhy: a number; no claim on the crunch

lines.quote: the demand is not there; it is still a supply shortage — a truck-driver shortage story; that is what is pushing up rates
lines.note: names a second object under the freight number: rates rise from labor, and the crunch rides along. The diesel is not the driver
lines.zWhy: rates rise from labor; the crunch rides along, not biting

lines.quote: all of the top line at J.B. Hunt was up 20%, including fuel surcharges — that is built on much higher rates
lines.note: THE PASS-THROUGH IN THE ACCOUNTS: the surcharge inside the revenue line; the crunch arrives as top-line growth. The line the cut exists for

lines.quote: they have a cost problem as well because of the driver shortage — signing bonuses, safety bonuses
lines.note: the cost side is labor, not fuel: the drivers bite, the diesel passes
lines.zWhy: the cost that bites is labor; by contrast the fuel passes

lines.quote: intermodal — truck to train for the long haul — is going great; it is about 65% more fuel-efficient than a truck, so it helps shippers; people want intermodal, and that will push up prices
lines.note: THE MECHANISM: the crunch routes shippers to the fuel-light mode and the price follows them there. Substitution, not shortage

lines.quote: contracts are negotiated on a yearly basis; they are underpriced right now, but bid season started in October — they will get higher prices and it will help margins
lines.note: dates the lag: the pass-through is contractual and arrives on the calendar
lines.zWhy: contractual repricing is pass-through with a calendar

lines.quote: intermodal up 20% year-over-year, loads themselves up 8.5% — that is healthy
lines.note: the activity side: volumes up, not down. No dent in the fuel-light mode
lines.zWhy: volumes up in the fuel-light mode: no dent

lines.quote: without a doubt — trucking rates and the spot market are up; that supports the increases in intermodal rates
lines.zWhy: rates up across modes: the price carries it
